option_relations.rationale: The clinical presentation and histopathological findings, including the presence of myeloperoxidase-positive cells, are consistent with leukemia cutis (myeloid sarcoma).
While Sweet's syndrome can present with similar skin lesions, the presence of myeloperoxidase-positive cells and the patient's history of multiple myeloma make it less likely.
Atypical/neutropenic Sweet syndrome is a variant of Sweet's syndrome, but the clinical and histopathological findings in this case are more consistent with leukemia cutis (myeloid sarcoma).
Histiocytoid Sweet syndrome is a rare variant of Sweet's syndrome, but the clinical and histopathological findings in this case are more consistent with leukemia cutis (myeloid sarcoma).
